Empirical Research Plan: “Lifetime Earnings Effects of Being Drafted in the Vietnam-Era U.S. Army”

====================================================================
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Chosen strategy: Instrumental-Variables / fuzzy Regression-Discontinuity design that uses the 1969–1972 draft lotteries.

Why appropriate  
• The draft lottery assigned a random number (1–365) to every date of birth within a cohort.  
• For each lottery year the Selective Service announced the highest number that would be inducted (call-up threshold).  
• Eligibility therefore jumps discontinuously at the threshold, but actual service is not deterministically forced (medical exemptions, deferments ⇒ “fuzzy” RD).  
• Using “DraftEligible” (lottery # ≤ threshold) as an instrument for “Served” gives a credible local average treatment effect (LATE) of military service on lifetime earnings.

Technically we will implement the design as a 2SLS with cohort fixed effects and, in robustness, a local linear fuzzy RD around each cohort-specific cutoff.

====================================================================
2. Treatment and Control
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable (endogenous)  
Served_i = 1 if individual i has any record of active-duty Vietnam-era military service; 0 otherwise.

Instrument / Eligibility indicator (first stage)  
Eligible_i = 1 if lottery number ≤ cohort-specific last called number, 0 otherwise.

Control group  
Men with lottery numbers above the call-up threshold (Eligible = 0). These men have the same birth-month distribution as the treated but a much lower probability of service.

Treatment timing / event date  
The “event” is induction, which occurs 0–12 months after the lottery drawing date. Because we use lifetime earnings, we do not model timing explicitly in the main 2SLS; however, for event-study robustness we index earnings relative to the calendar year of the lottery.

Running variable and cutoff (for RD robustness)  
Running: LotteryNumber_i ∈ [1,365].  
Cutoff: C_y, the highest number called in lottery year y (different y have different C_y). The design is fuzzy because P(Served) jumps but not from 0 to 1.

====================================================================
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Random assignment of lottery numbers (Independence)  
The lottery was televised and mechanically random ⇒ birth-date is effectively random with respect to potential earnings. Highly plausible.

A2. First-stage relevance  
Eligibility strongly raises the probability of service. Historic call-up rates 50–60 p.p. difference across threshold indicate a powerful first stage. Check in data.

A3. Exclusion restriction  
Lottery eligibility affects lifetime earnings only through actual military service (no direct channel). Plausible because deferments, education decisions, etc. are triggered by the prospect of service; we will test for “education channel” by controlling for education in robustness.

A4. Monotonicity / no defiers  
No one who would serve if ineligible would refuse to serve if eligible. Institutional rules (cannot volunteer if not eligible) support this.

A5. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA)  
One man’s eligibility does not affect another’s earnings directly. Plausible given huge population and individual-level outcome.

====================================================================
4. Main Threats and Remedies
--------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Selective non-compliance (medical deferments, college deferments)  
• Show first-stage strength across observable sub-groups.  
• Estimate complier characteristics using Abadie (2003) method.  
• Present bounds using Manski-Lee.

T2. Differential attrition / missing SSA earnings (migration, death, self-employment not reported)  
• Verify balance in SSA coverage rates across eligibility near threshold.  
• Re-weight by inverse probability of being observed.  
• Use IRS wage files (if accessible) for robustness.

T3. Other channels violating exclusion (education, marriage, GI Bill)  
• Report reduced-form effect of eligibility on education and marriage to gauge magnitude.  
• Control flexibly for years of schooling at second stage — show coefficient on Served robust.  
• Implement a “placebo” instrument using next-year lottery numbers to test for anticipatory schooling.

====================================================================
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
#--------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
#--------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(fixest)       # IV regressions
library(rdrobust)     # fuzzy RD robustness
library(ggplot2)

#--------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
#--------------------------------------------------
# Assume file "ssa_vietnam.csv" is in working directory
dt <- fread("ssa_vietnam.csv")

#--------------------------------------------------
# 2. Variable construction
#--------------------------------------------------
# cohort-specific cutoff vector imported from separate file or coded manually
cutoff_df <- data.table(lottery_year = 1969:1972,
                        cutoff       = c(195,215,125,95))  # example values
dt <- merge(dt, cutoff_df, by = "lottery_year", all.x = TRUE)

dt[, Eligible := as.integer(lottery_number <= cutoff)]
dt[, Served   := as.integer(served == 1)]  # ensure 0/1
# Lifetime earnings: sum real earnings 1968–1988 (example window)
earn_vars <- paste0("earn_", 1968:1988)
dt[, lifetime_earn := rowSums(.SD, na.rm = TRUE), .SDcols = earn_vars]

#--------------------------------------------------
# 3. Main specification: 2SLS
#--------------------------------------------------
iv_main <- feols(lifetime_earn ~ 1 | Served ~ Eligible | 
                 cohort + birth_year,  # fixed effects
                 data = dt, cluster = ~lottery_number)
summary(iv_main)

#--------------------------------------------------
# 4. First-stage strength check
#--------------------------------------------------
fs <- feols(Served ~ Eligible | cohort + birth_year, 
            data = dt, cluster = ~lottery_number)
summary(fs)

#--------------------------------------------------
# 5. Fuzzy RD robustness (local linear ±25 lottery numbers)
#--------------------------------------------------
rd_sample <- dt[abs(lottery_number - cutoff) <= 25]
rd <- rdrobust(y = rd_sample$lifetime_earn,
               x = rd_sample$lottery_number - rd_sample$cutoff,
               fuzzy = rd_sample$Served)
summary(rd)

#--------------------------------------------------
# 6. Covariate balance plot
#--------------------------------------------------
covs <- c("white", "black", "hispanic", "mom_education")
bal <- lapply(covs, function(v){
  feols(as.formula(paste(v, "~ Eligible")), data=dt)$coeftable[2,]
})
print(bal)
```

====================================================================
6. Expected Results
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Economic theory is ambiguous (human-capital loss from time out of the labor market vs. subsidised college via GI Bill, veterans’ preference). Prior empirical work on WWII veterans suggests small negative or zero long-run effects. I expect:  
• Point estimate: ‑5 % to ‑10 % lower cumulative real earnings (≈ −$40k to −$80k in 1984 $) for compliers.  
• Heterogeneity: larger losses for college-educated potential servicemen, little effect for low-skill men.

====================================================================
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (IV design)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: Random assignment of instrument .................................... 1  
C2: Strong first stage (F-stat > 10) ................................... 1  
C3: Exclusion restriction (no direct path) ............................. 0.5  
C4: Monotonicity (no defiers) .......................................... 1  
C5: No interference / SUTVA ............................................ 0.8  
Total (out of 5) = 4.3

====================================================================
End of Plan
